question.prompt: The vertices of a quadrilateral lie on the graph of \(y = \ln x,\) and the \(x\)-coordinates of these vertices are consecutive positive integers. The area of the quadrilateral is \(\ln\dfrac{91}{90}.\) What is the \(x\)-coordinate of the leftmost vertex?

solutions.title: Subtract trapezoid areas
solutions.explanation:
The consecutive \(x\)-coordinates give three strips of width \(1\), making trapezoid areas convenient.

Let the leftmost coordinate be the positive integer \(n\), and write
\[
y_0=\ln n,\quad y_1=\ln(n+1),\quad y_2=\ln(n+2),\quad y_3=\ln(n+3).
\]
Call the corresponding vertices \(A,B,C,D\), in increasing order of \(x\).

The slopes of \(AB,BC,CD\) are
\[
\ln\left(1+\frac1n\right),\quad
\ln\left(1+\frac1{n+1}\right),\quad
\ln\left(1+\frac1{n+2}\right).
\]
They strictly decrease because \(\ln x\) is increasing. Thus the broken line \(ABCD\) bends downward, with \(B\) and \(C\) above the closing segment \(AD\).

The area below the three upper segments and above the \(x\)-axis is, by the trapezoid formula,
\[
T=\frac{y_0+y_1}{2}+\frac{y_1+y_2}{2}+\frac{y_2+y_3}{2}.
\]
The area below \(AD\) over the same horizontal interval is
\[
U=\frac{3(y_0+y_3)}2.
\]
Subtracting gives the quadrilateral's area:
\[
\begin{aligned}
T-U&=y_1+y_2-y_0-y_3\\
&=\ln\frac{(n+1)(n+2)}{n(n+3)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Equate this to the given area. Equal natural logarithms have equal positive arguments, so
\[
\frac{(n+1)(n+2)}{n(n+3)}=\frac{91}{90}.
\]
Since \((n+1)(n+2)=n(n+3)+2\), this becomes
\[
1+\frac2{n(n+3)}=1+\frac1{90}.
\]
Hence
\[
n^2+3n=180,
\qquad (n-12)(n+15)=0.
\]
Only the positive root is allowed. The leftmost \(x\)-coordinate is \(\boxed{12}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).

solutions.title: Use the shoelace formula
solutions.explanation:
A horizontal translation makes the four \(x\)-coordinates \(0,1,2,3\), which simplifies the shoelace calculation without changing area.

Let \(n\) be the leftmost original \(x\)-coordinate, and define \(y_i=\ln(n+i)\) for \(i=0,1,2,3\). The translated vertices are
\[
(0,y_0),\quad(1,y_1),\quad(2,y_2),\quad(3,y_3).
\]
Their successive slopes are \(\ln(1+1/(n+i))\) for \(i=0,1,2\). These strictly decrease, so visiting the vertices in the displayed order and returning to the first follows the convex quadrilateral's boundary.

The shoelace formula gives polygon area as half the absolute difference between the sums of the forward and backward coordinate products. Thus the area \(S\) is
\[
\begin{aligned}
S&=\frac12\left|(y_2+2y_3+3y_0)-(y_0+2y_1+3y_2)\right|\\
&=\left|y_1+y_2-y_0-y_3\right|\\
&=\left|\ln\frac{(n+1)(n+2)}{n(n+3)}\right|.
\end{aligned}
\]
The numerator exceeds the denominator by \(2\), so the logarithm is positive. Therefore
\[
\ln\frac{(n+1)(n+2)}{n(n+3)}=\ln\frac{91}{90}.
\]
Equating the arguments and using \((n+1)(n+2)=n(n+3)+2\), we obtain
\[
1+\frac2{n(n+3)}=\frac{91}{90},
\qquad n(n+3)=180.
\]
Consequently,
\[
n^2+3n-180=(n-12)(n+15)=0.
\]
Since \(n\) is positive, the answer is \(\boxed{12}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
